chatter verb

also my teeth are chattering, teeth chattering, gossip (chatter)

classical

Traupman 323

garriō, garrīre

verb, fourth conjugation

Other words

  • dentibus crepitāre — (of teeth) chatter

    also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 2.6.52; Lucr. 5.746 (Lewis & Short s.v. crepitō); Traupman 289

    Literally “to rattle with the teeth”: dentibus crepitō, my teeth are chattering.

  • balbūtiō, balbūtīre — stammer, stutter (not chatter)

    verb, fourth conjugation · avoid · classical · Traupman 289

    Traupman gives it for “chatter”; Lewis & Short: “to stammer, stutter”. For chattering teeth Latin says dentibus crepitāre.

Examples

  • garrīmus quicquid in buccam

    we chatter about whatever comes to mindCic. Att. XII 1, 2
